clue.text: Some stopped, largely to see travelling salesman

indicators.note: only some of the following letters are wanted, a run lying inside the words that follow

blocks.note: the run straddles the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: Somebody was stopped mostly so they could meet a door-to-door salesman.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedlar is a hawker who goes from place to place selling small goods.

clue.text: Calm, I start to feel, during fast

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, so only that is kept
something happening during another thing sits within it, so these letters go inside

blocks.note: pacy means quick
taken as written
opening letter of feel

explanation.surface: Someone describes calming down by beginning to feel things while fasting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fast' looks like going without food, but it means quick; the pair I and F goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To pacify is to soothe or quieten someone, so the verb works as a synonym of calm.

clue.text: Polite and appropriate, showing luggage from embassy?

blocks.note: tactful and courteous
as a verb, to bag something is to take it for yourself

explanation.surface: Courteous and fitting behaviour is on display in luggage from an embassy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Appropriate' reads as an adjective meaning suitable, but here it is the verb: to seize.
explanation.definitionFit: A diplomatic bag is the sealed container an embassy uses to send items exempt from customs searches; the question mark flags the loose wording.

clue.text: Small explosion a little after noon — drive off

blocks.note: a little after noon is at one o'clock: AT plus the Roman numeral I
shoo is what you say to chase an animal away

explanation.surface: A small blast goes off shortly after midday, and someone drives away.
explanation.walkthrough: A little after noon is 'at one', with one written as the Roman numeral I; then add the word for chasing an animal away.
explanation.definitionFit: Atishoo is the written sound of a sneeze, jokingly described here as a small explosion from the nose.

clue.text: Small impression made by streak

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a print is a mark pressed into a surface

explanation.surface: A faint mark is left behind by a streak of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Streak' looks like a noun for a stripe, but it is the verb: to run very fast.
explanation.definitionFit: To sprint is to run at full speed, and to streak is likewise to dash past quickly.

clue.text: Small pet I left for schoolchild

blocks.note: a young dog, a small pet
taken as written
L is the standard abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Someone leaves their little pet behind for a schoolchild to look after.
explanation.definitionFit: A pupil is a child being taught at school, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Impersonator of Manet, for example

blocks.note: first meaning: an entertainer who mimics famous people
second meaning: a painter of the French movement led by Monet, Manet and others

explanation.surface: Someone does an impression of the French painter Manet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Of' joins the two meanings, making it look like a single impression of one painter.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a stage mimic and a member of the 19th-century French art movement, of which Manet is an example.

clue.text: In field accommodation, a new occupant

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it, so the following pair is placed within

blocks.note: a tent is shelter put up in a field
taken as written
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A new occupant arrives in accommodation out in a field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' heads the clue as if describing location; it puts A and N inside the field shelter.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenant is a person who occupies a property, usually paying rent, so tenant and occupant are synonyms.

clue.text: Officer briefly backing the best legend

indicators.note: something backing up goes in reverse, so these letters run the other way

blocks.note: the short form of the rank captain
the best is number one, written NO I

explanation.surface: A senior officer quickly gives backing to the best legend of all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Legend' suggests a famous person, but it means the words printed under a picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A legend in printing is the explanatory text beneath an illustration or map, the same as a caption.

clue.text: Breaking egg, linnet is careless

indicators.note: breaking smashes something into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A songbird that breaks an egg is being careless.
explanation.walkthrough: A linnet is a small finch, which makes the picture of a bird with an egg natural.
explanation.definitionFit: Negligent describes someone who fails to take proper care, the same sense as careless.

clue.text: Dad at home? Make quick visit

blocks.note: pop is an informal name for father
someone who is in is at home

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether Dad is at home, so they can call by briefly.
explanation.definitionFit: To pop in is to make a short informal call on someone, matching a quick visit.

clue.text: Foam moving forth

indicators.note: letters that are moving are shifted into new places

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Foam is moving forward, perhaps a wave spilling up a beach.
explanation.definitionFit: Froth is a mass of small bubbles on a liquid, which is a synonym of foam.

clue.text: All gone to repair sailing ship

indicators.note: something sent to repair is broken and must be put back together differently

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Everyone has left to mend an old sailing vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A galleon is a large multi-decked sailing vessel used by Spain and others from the 15th to 18th centuries.

clue.text: Gets rid of a book he soils badly

indicators.note: something done badly is botched, so the letters end up in the wrong order

blocks.note: taken as written
B is the abbreviation for book
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man gets rid of a book after making a dirty mess of it.
explanation.definitionFit: To abolish is to do away with something entirely, so abolishes matches gets rid of.

clue.text: Fish eggs the boat race teams have, it's said

indicators.note: something said is spoken, so the spelling matters less than the sound

blocks.note: the crews in the Boat Race have a hard row, a gruelling stretch of rowing

explanation.surface: The rowing crews dine on fish eggs, or so people say.
explanation.walkthrough: The Boat Race is the annual rowing contest on the Thames between Oxford and Cambridge universities.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard roe is the mass of eggs in a female fish, as opposed to soft roe, the male's milt.

clue.text: Foreman's error? Right!

blocks.note: a gaffe is a blunder
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether the foreman made a mistake, and is told yes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foreman's' looks possessive, but the 's stands for 'is' and joins definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaffer is informal British for a boss, especially the foreman in charge of workers.

clue.text: English visiting very pleasant city

indicators.note: a visitor goes inside someone else's place, so this letter is placed within

blocks.note: V is the abbreviation for very
nice means pleasant
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: An English tourist visits a very lovely city.
explanation.walkthrough: Nice is also a city, which tempts the solver to stop there; the visiting English letter goes inside after V.
explanation.definitionFit: Venice is the Italian city of canals, an example of a city.

clue.text: In dispute, what's needed for a 3?

definitions.note: read as the phrase A TISSUE, a noun

blocks.note: first meaning: being argued over
second meaning: 3-down is a sneeze, and for that you need a paper handkerchief

explanation.walkthrough: The 3 refers to the answer of 3-down, a sneeze; split the answer differently and it becomes what you reach for afterwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A matter at issue is the one under debate, so it is in dispute; split differently it is a paper handkerchief.

clue.text: European married in Suez, oddly

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters are the first, third and so on, so every other one is kept
one thing in another sits inside it, so the married word goes within

blocks.note: first and third letters of Suez
wed means married

explanation.surface: A European got married in Suez, which was rather strange.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oddly' seems to comment on the wedding, but it picks the odd letters of Suez.
explanation.definitionFit: A Swede is a person from Sweden, so is one example of a European.

clue.text: Run hard alongside one river

blocks.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard
taken as written

explanation.surface: A runner goes hard beside a single river.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rhone is a major river flowing from Switzerland through France to the Mediterranean.

clue.text: Untrue statement about roughage

blocks.note: a fib is a small lie
re means concerning

explanation.surface: Somebody tells a lie about how much roughage they eat.
explanation.definitionFit: Dietary fibre is the indigestible plant matter also called roughage.

clue.text: Some shorter miniskirts, the ends of lines

indicators.note: only some of the following letters are wanted, a run inside the words

blocks.note: the run straddles the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: Some shorter skirts are the end of the line for fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lines' suggests hemlines, but it means railway lines.
explanation.definitionFit: Termini are the stations at the end of railway or bus routes, the plural of terminus.

clue.text: Covered in carpet, very hard-wearing

blocks.note: first meaning: furnished with rugs
second meaning: tough and durable

explanation.walkthrough: The first meaning is a whimsical one, reading the word as 'having rugs put down'.
explanation.definitionFit: Rugged usually means sturdy and durable, and can also be read jokingly as fitted with rugs.

clue.text: Watch article boil

blocks.note: to see is to watch
the definite article

explanation.surface: Someone watches an item come to the boil.
explanation.definitionFit: To seethe is to bubble violently, the action of a liquid that is boiling.
